title.narrative: Output A.1. Enhanced decent work statistics using innovative sources and statistical standards

description.narrative:
The Government of South Africa, in collaboration with the National Statistics Office (Statistics South Africa - Statssa) developed and adopted a Labour Market Information System in June 2023 that was launched in November 2023. The LMIS provides the country with the necessary tools to evaluate the labour market experience of men and women. The data displayed in the LMIS falls within the Decent Work Framework that includes groupings of indicators measuring ‘Equal Opportunities and treatment at work’ to reflect and compare the experiences of women and men in the labour market. LMIS makes use of data from different sources and these data are based on Statistical Standards. Data derived from the Quarterly Labour Force is based on 19th ICLS Resolution.
In February 2022 the Government of South Africa, through Statistics South Africa, conducted the Population and Housing Census 2022 that integrated the ILO Model questionnaire for Census that allows Census data to produce labour market statistics. The ILO Model questionnaire aligns to the 19th International Conference of Labour Statisticians Resolution on Work, Employment and Labour Underutilization. With the contributions from RBTC, the ILO provided capacity building support to Government throughout the entire process of developing the Labour Market Information System. This support was provided through three workshops, two of which were held in the previous biennium and the third held in May 2022. In the third workshop held in May 2022, the ILO provided training on data preparation and uploading. The key purpose of this workshop was to train staff on how to upload data and manage the LMIS platform. In March 2023, the ILO supported the LMIS Unit at the National Department of Employment & Labour to install the LMIS.STAT application software. In June 2023, the ITC-ILO collaborated with the ILO to run a special workshop organized for countries about to launch their respective LMIS including those from South Africa. LMIS staff from the National Department of Employment and Labour attended this workshop.
In January 2022 the ILO provided support to Statistics South Africa in reviewing and contributing towards questionnaire design of the Population and Housing Census 2022, including the integration of the ILO’s Model Questionnaire for Census. Support was also provided ensuring the inclusion of disability and labour migration modules in the Census.
